subject: Mathematics
source: Original supplementary learning draft aligned to Class 6 Ganita Prakash Chapter 9 (fegp109.pdf), Reprint 2026–27. Verify any school-specific edition before publication.
goals: Test symmetry by folding or matching corresponding points.
Distinguish symmetry from general visual balance.
summary: A figure has line symmetry when it can be folded along a line so that the two halves match exactly. Rotational symmetry describes whether a figure matches itself after a turn smaller than a full turn.

concepts.title: Line symmetry
concepts.explanation: A line of symmetry divides a figure into two mirror-image halves. Every point on one side has a corresponding point at the same perpendicular distance on the other side.
concepts.example: A square has four lines of symmetry: two through the midpoints of opposite sides and two diagonals.

concepts.title: Testing symmetry
concepts.explanation: Imagine folding the figure along a candidate line. If both halves match exactly, the line is a symmetry line. A drawing may look balanced without having exact symmetry.
concepts.example: A scalene triangle has no line of symmetry because no fold makes its sides and vertices match.

concepts.title: Rotational symmetry
concepts.explanation: A figure has rotational symmetry if a turn less than 360° maps it onto itself. The smallest positive such angle is the angle of rotation.
concepts.example: A square matches itself after a 90° turn around its centre.

concepts.title: Symmetry in designs
concepts.explanation: Symmetry appears in patterns, tiles, leaves, architecture and logos. Identifying the exact transformation helps describe a design mathematically.
concepts.example: A repeated border may have translation symmetry even if a single motif has a line of symmetry.

workedExamples.question: How many lines of symmetry does a non-square rectangle have?
steps: Try folding vertically through its centre: halves match.
Try folding horizontally through its centre: halves match.
A diagonal fold does not generally match.

workedExamples.question: Does an equilateral triangle have line symmetry?
steps: Each vertex can be joined to the midpoint of the opposite side.
Each of these three lines divides the triangle into matching halves.
workedExamples.answer: Yes, it has three lines of symmetry.

practice.question: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
practice.why: Two through side midpoints and two along diagonals.

practice.question: Does a scalene triangle have a line of symmetry?
practice.why: Its three side lengths differ, so no fold creates matching halves.

practice.question: What does rotational symmetry mean?
practice.answer: A figure maps onto itself after a turn smaller than 360°.
practice.why: The figure’s appearance matches after the rotation.

practice.question: Why is a visual guess not always enough to identify symmetry?
practice.answer: A figure can look balanced while its halves do not match exactly.
practice.why: Symmetry is an exact geometric relationship.

mcqs.why: The halves match as mirror images.

mcqs.q: A square has how many lines of symmetry?
mcqs.why: A square has four reflection axes.
No sides or angles match in a way that permits a symmetry fold.
Rotation is a turn around a centre.

mcqs.q: A square maps onto itself after a 90° turn. This shows…
mcqs.why: A quarter-turn maps the square to the same outline.

revision: Line symmetry means the halves match as mirror images.
A square has 4 lines of symmetry; a rectangle that is not a square has 2.
An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry; a scalene triangle has none.
Rotational symmetry occurs when a turn smaller than 360° maps the figure onto itself.

chapterTest.instructions: Answer independently before opening the answer guide. Show steps for calculations.

questions.q: Describe a way to test a proposed line of symmetry.
questions.answer: Fold along it or compare corresponding points; the two halves must match exactly.

questions.q: Compare line symmetry in a square and a non-square rectangle.
questions.answer: A square has four lines of symmetry; a non-square rectangle has two.

questions.q: What is rotational symmetry? Give an example.
questions.answer: A figure matches itself after a turn smaller than 360°; a square matches after a 90° turn.
